This PR includes several changes to the discharge evaluation in GEB. The most important change is that we now report both the traditional KGE as the modified KGE, alongside many more skill scores. Moreover, we support a comparison of GEB to external models (e.g. Google), including automatic matching of GRDC stations. The main changes were the following: 

- Added optional external discharge skill-score comparisons for Google Streamflow, GloFAS, and PCR-GLOBWB/Utrecht.
- Expanded discharge metrics with original/modified KGE, KGE components, NSE, Pearson r², RMSE, and RRMSE.
- Added skill-score maps, boxplots, external KGE comparisons, upstream-area diagnostics, and dashboard summaries.
- Improved the interactive discharge evaluation dashboard, and remove the option for static dashboards. 

The discharge evaluation scripts are now getting long and the advancements require a large restructuring of the evaluate/hydrology.py in the near future.

  • SciPy now supports three different build modes for BLAS and LAPACK LP64/ILP64 support, and machinery is provided for downstream cython_lapack consumers to gracefully handle LP64/ILP64 backend builds. ILP64 support has been substantially improved across the SciPy library.

  • SciPy's internal FFT backend has switched from pocketfft to its successor package ducc0.fft, which features several incremental improvements. title: Tim europe model evaluation updates
body:
Closes #162 

This PR contains many improvements to the evaluation, specifically of discharge. Moreover, we now support a new tool (geb tool merge) to automatically merge many different GEB sub-models into one new model. This merged model can then be evaluated using regular evaluation methods. Specifically, this PR added the following: 
1)	Add `geb tool merge` command to merge outputs from multiple GEB cluster sub-models into a single merged model directory that can be evaluated directly with `geb evaluate`.
2)	Add `plot_skill_score_maps()` to plot skill scores per station on a satellite basemap for each metric.
3)	Update `plot_skill_score_boxplots()` with violin + boxplot panels for KGE, NSE, R², RMSE and RRMSE, including support for overlaying external reference model (e.g. LISFLOOD) results.
4)	Add R², RMSE and RRMSE to discharge evaluation metrics at hourly, daily and monthly frequencies.
5)	Stations with fewer than 5 years of paired observations are skipped in `evaluate_discharge`. This setting, as well as an upstream area threshold for evaluation, is part of the reasonable default confg. 
6)	Lakes and reservoirs are now shown as dot markers in the interactive discharge evaluation map.
7)	 Add regression plots between the upstream area and the skill scores (one plot for each score).

title: Jens industry water demand
body:
- Abstraction from industry is now assumed to be abstracted from larger rivers only. If we let industry abstract from each grid cell that has any industry, the industrial users abstract water from very small rivers, which also leads to very high groundwater abstraction in those cells because the demand is not satisfiable from the river. This is highly unrealistic. Therefore, we define abstraction areas based on the river network. Each abstraction area is associated with a river of shreve stream order above a set threshold. All water demands from industry are essentially transferred downstream to the river of the abstraction area, and abstraction is assumed to occur from that river.
- All other configuration options that essentially tried to do some of these things above per study area (like custom abstraction) are removed now. Hopefully we can simply reduce the need for configuration options with better defaults!
- Change units that industry and livestock water demand return (now m3/day, was m/day).
